original_test_intent: Verify the Bus Number component of each Type 9 optional PCI slot address belongs to the approved segment:bus:device.function mapping, uses the defined unknown/not-applicable tuple only where allowed, and remains correct after reboot under an unchanged topology.
original_method: Validate Type 9 record length, extract raw segment, bus and device/function bytes atomically, bind the canonical tuple to the exact slot, correlate with the approved firmware/OS PCI map and repeat after reboot.
manual_activity: A user approves the slot-to-PCI bus map, acceptable enumeration stability and reboot plan. No device rebinding or bus reassignment is part of the case.
required_inputs: Expected bus number within the full PCI tuple per Type 9 slot
Applicable SMBIOS version/record length and sentinel semantics
Policy for empty slots and whether firmware bus numbering must remain stable across the approved reboot
Validated raw parser, read-only PCI inventory and reboot/OOB recovery plan
safety_requirements: Use read-only SMBIOS and PCI enumeration; do not rescan destructively, bind/unbind devices or change topology/firmware.
Preserve the raw bus byte and complete address tuple; bus 00 is a valid value and must not be confused with missing data.
Apply the specification-defined unknown/not-applicable sentinel only as the complete address condition, not to an isolated bus byte.
Record the unchanged hardware and firmware configuration because PCI bus numbering can depend on topology and resource allocation.
Stop on partial/malformed tuples, unexpected renumbering or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Extract the raw bus byte from length-valid Type 9 records, construct the complete canonical tuple, correlate it with read-only PCI inventory and compare pre/post reboot.
Do not change PCI state or issue PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the expected bus/tuple map, sentinel policy and acceptable enumeration stability.
Approve reboot/recovery, adjudicate any valid platform renumbering and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A literal `Bus Num` grep may miss common `Bus Address` output and cannot distinguish bus zero, a sentinel tuple or an inconsistent segment/device/function combination.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive complete raw/decoded Type 9 records and report the raw bus byte only within the length-validated segment:bus:device.function tuple, with slot identity and read-only OS correlation.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Bus Num scope, Type 9 script and 5/5-minute values are retained; the legacy grep is preserved but not relied upon.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Parse the Type 9 address extension from raw data, retain bus byte and full canonical PCI tuple, distinguish valid 00 from the complete unknown sentinel and compare the topology/map across reboot.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 9 records with the PCI address extension.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, BIOS, Type 9 length, OS and parser/PCI-tool versions plus topology identity.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 9 Bus Number and address-tuple layout, approved PCI topology map and installed tool documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces an unreliable isolated grep with record-length-aware tuple parsing and explicit zero/sentinel handling.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; detects partial tuple errors and valid-versus-missing bus ambiguity while supporting OS correlation.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Per-slot tuple map and enumeration stability/sentinel policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Bus numbers may legitimately change when topology, firmware configuration or resource allocation changes; such a change invalidates a simple persistence baseline.

project_override_considerations: A project may accept a documented renumbering only when the approved topology/resource change is part of the plan; it must retain the complete old/new tuple and cannot declare isolated bus equality sufficient.
expected_evidence: Approved topology, per-slot bus/tuple map, stability rule and SMBIOS sentinel policy
Complete pre-reboot Type 9 records with structure length, slot identity, raw address bytes and canonical tuple
Read-only OS PCI domain/BDF inventory and per-slot correlation or approved sentinel result
Approved reboot/health and unchanged-topology evidence plus post-reboot tuple diff

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Bus Num is an abbreviated but clear reference to the canonical Type 9 Bus Number component.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Length-aware raw parsing and read-only PCI correlation safely resolve the value; pending maps are readiness inputs.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Corrects an unreliable isolated label and adds bus-zero, sentinel and complete-tuple semantics.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains PCI mapping safeguards while restoring FULLY AUTOMATABLE classification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates topology inputs, reboot approval and engineer verdict from execution capability.

review_improvement: Prevents valid bus 00 from being treated as absent and prevents an isolated correct bus byte from hiding a wrong segment or device/function component.
independent_technical_reasoning: The Bus Number is a raw byte in the optional Type 9 address tuple; with record-length and topology rules, extraction and correlation are deterministic software operations.
